\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}
This note records two elementary facts about even integers. It exists so
that the evaluation harness has a small paper with theorem environments.

\section{Even integers}
\label{sec:even}

\begin{definition}
\label{def:even}
An integer $n$ is \emph{even} if $n = 2k$ for some integer $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:sum}
If $a$ and $b$ are even in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:even}, then
$a + b$ is even.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
By Definition~\ref{def:even} write $a = 2j$ and $b = 2k$. Then
$a + b = 2(j + k)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:finite-sum}
Let $m \geq 1$ and let $a_1, \dots, a_m$ be even in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:even}. Then $a_1 + \dots + a_m$ is even.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Induction on $m$. For $m = 1$ there is nothing to show. If the claim holds
for $m$, then $a_1 + \dots + a_m$ is even, and adding $a_{m+1}$ gives an
even integer by Lemma~\ref{lem:sum}.
\end{proof}
